similarities.summary: Distributions share 77.5% overlap across the p10-p90 range (≥40% threshold). Moon South Pole crater rim and ejecta blockiness (3.2-13.8% area, median 7.4%) operationally matches Atacama desert pavement gravel and cobble density (4.5-15.2%, median 9.5%). Rover wheel clearance and trafficability limits (<15% rock cover) are directly analogous.

candidate_stats.source: Atacama Desert Pavement Surface Rock Fraction Photogrammetry

target_stats.source: LRO Diviner Rock Abundance Map (Bandfield et al. 2011)

similarities.direction_note: Surface boulder coverage is within rover mobility tolerance on both bodies.

mismatches.summary: Mineral suites are completely disjoint. Moon South Pole is ancient anorthositic crust (>90% calcic plagioclase feldspar) with cold-trapped water ice volatiles in PSRs. Atacama exhibits hyper-arid sedimentary evaporites (gypsum, halite, anhydrite) and phyllosilicates. No basaltic or anorthositic analogue lithology.
mismatches.direction_note: Igneous crust vs terrestrial sedimentary/evaporite suite.
mismatches.detail: Diviner Christiansen Feature (CF) identifies anorthosite; Atacama shows terrestrial evaporite spectra.

mismatches.summary: Earth Atacama shows aeolian deflation and trace evaporite alteration (gypsum, halite). Target surface has no atmospheric weathering — only micrometeorite comminution (Moon) or aeolian perchlorate chemistry (Mars). Earth soil is weathered; target regolith is pristine or reactive.

evidence.summary: Region not found in crosswalk. Manual classification required.

mismatches.summary: Distributions share 0.0% overlap (completely disjoint). Moon South Pole exhibits extreme cryogenic conditions: Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) remain constantly at 38-60 K (<40 K cold traps), while sunlit polar rims reach at most 210 K. Atacama median is 288 K (+15°C); Moon polar median is 85 K (-188°C).

candidate_stats.source: Atacama Surface Weather Station & MODIS Land Surface Temperature

target_stats.source: LRO Diviner Polar Brightness Temperature (Paige et al. 2010)

mismatches.direction_note: Moon South Pole is 186 K colder on median than Atacama.

mismatches.summary: Distributions overlap only 8.0% across the p10-p90 range. On the Moon, illuminated polar crater rims experience diurnal swings up to 175 K, while PSR crater floors experience zero swing (continuous cryogenic stasis). Earth diurnal swing is tightly buffered at 22-36 K by atmospheric convective heat flux.

candidate_stats.source: Atacama Annual Diurnal Temperature Swing (Max - Min)

target_stats.source: LRO Diviner Polar Diurnal Thermal Amplitude (Williams et al. 2017)

mismatches.direction_note: Moon diurnal swings are unbuffered by atmosphere.

mismatches.summary: Distributions share 0.0% overlap (completely disjoint). Lunar fine regolith in vacuum has exceptionally low thermal inertia (35-85 TIU) due to lack of interstitial gas conduction. Atacama desert pavement is consolidated with interstitial air, yielding 280-720 TIU.

candidate_stats.source: Atacama Desert Pavement Soil & Gravel Thermal Inertia

target_stats.source: Lunar Regolith Thermal Inertia Map (Hayne et al. 2017)

mismatches.direction_note: Lunar regolith has 8x lower thermal inertia than terrestrial desert pavement.

mismatches.summary: Direct cross-body temperature comparison is subject to fundamental atmospheric physics disparity: Earth has a 1,013 hPa convective boundary layer; Mars has ~6 hPa CO₂ with weak convective coupling; Moon is hard vacuum (~10⁻¹² hPa) with purely radiative heat transfer.

Distributions overlap only 5.3% across the p10-p90 range. Moon South Pole exhibits an extreme bimodal regime: 18% permanently shadowed regions (0.0 fraction, <40 K cold traps) adjacent to elevated crater rims (up to 0.86). Atacama has a uniform diurnal daylight fraction (~0.51).

candidate_stats.source: Analytical Spherical Astronomy & Atacama Clear-Sky Solar Geometry

target_stats.source: LRO LOLA 4 ppd Polar Illumination Map (Mazarico et al. 2011)

mismatches.direction_note: Moon polar illumination is bimodal and topography-shadowed; Earth is unimodal diurnal.

mismatches.summary: Moon South Pole solar elevation never exceeds ±1.5° above horizon (obliquity 1.54°). Sunlight grazes the surface, casting horizon-scale multi-kilometer shadows. Atacama solar elevation reaches 89.5° at solar noon with minimal shadowing.
mismatches.direction_note: Solar elevation ranges are completely disjoint (Earth up to 89.5°, Moon max 1.5°).

mismatches.summary: Earth operates on a 24.0h diurnal day/night rotation cycle. Moon South Pole lacks a diurnal cycle: sun circles the local horizon continuously without setting during polar summer and stays submerged in polar winter. Rotational physics are incomparable.
mismatches.direction_note: Earth 24.0h diurnal cycle vs Lunar polar azimuth-precessing grazing sun.

data_quality.candidate_source: NASA SRTM GL1 1-arcsecond window N41W122 at 41.6532, -121.0132 (64 x 64 cells, 27 m/px), measured by the screening pass
data_quality.target_source: Smith et al. (2010). Initial observations from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA). GRL.
data_quality.common_baseline_note: No resampling performed. Resolution disparity documented in uncertainties.
data_quality.slope_roughness_source: Pre-computed by Abid T S terrain.py pipeline (commit ab3228f)

uncertainties: Resolution disparity is the dominant uncertainty: candidate at 27 m/px captures sub-km terrain; target at 7.6 km/px averages landscape-scale features.
Thermal and surface rock evaluations reflect LRO Diviner polar radiometry and Mars 2020 MEDA / TES records; seasonal subsurface heat conduction models remain pending.
Geological crosswalk is a draft built from map group names only. Full unit descriptions have not been verified.
Illumination comparison reflects regional LOLA polar fraction; local horizon line-of-sight raytracing is required for specific landing sites.

limitations.impact: Slope stability, avalanche dynamics, and rover traction differ fundamentally. Equal slope angles are NOT equally hazardous across bodies.
No convective heat dissipation, no liquid water stability, no atmospheric pressure on suits or habitats.

limitations.target: Direct GCR and solar particle events (no magnetospheric shielding)
limitations.impact: Surface habitats require regolith berming or sub-surface siting. No Earth analogue preparation addresses this.

limitations.earth: Active microbial, hydro-chemical, and aeolian weathering
limitations.target: Micrometeorite comminution only; no atmospheric weathering; glassy electrostatic agglutinates
limitations.impact: Earth regolith contains organic binders. Target body regolith is mechanically abrasive or chemically hazardous.
